lead: Wisconsin homes face basement floods, frozen pipes and big summer storms. DryFlare helps owners from Milwaukee to Madison and Green Bay get water out and dry.
risk: basement flooding from heavy rain, frozen pipes and ice dams
risk_short: basement floods, frozen pipes, ice dams
why: In August 2024, Milwaukee got more than 10 inches of rain in parts of the city in about a day. Basements flooded across the metro, and sewers backed up. In 2008, floods drained Lake Delton and hit towns across southern Wisconsin.

Winter brings frozen pipes and ice dams, especially in the north. Most Wisconsin homes have basements, and over half were built before 1980. Old drain tile and foundations let water in during snowmelt and heavy rain. Minnesota, Michigan and Illinois share these risks.
image_alt: Water covering a basement floor after heavy rain
image_caption: Heavy summer rain can overwhelm sewers and flood basements across Milwaukee.
tips: Test your sump pump before spring melt and add a backup.
Install a backwater valve on the basement floor drain.
Add attic insulation to cut ice dams.
Keep the heat on in cabins or drain the plumbing.
insurance: Sewer backup and sump pump failure need a water backup endorsement on most Wisconsin policies.

faq.q: Is basement flooding from heavy rain covered in Wisconsin?
faq.a: It depends on how the water got in. Sewer backup is covered only with water backup cover. Water seeping through walls from the ground is often excluded. Surface flooding needs flood insurance. Check your policy.

licensing_faq: Contractors who pull building permits for homes in Wisconsin need a credential from the Department of Safety and Professional Services. Plumbers and electricians need state licenses.
